# ADR-0002: Multi-Module Gradle Structure (core / html / android)

<!-- Generated by seed-golden-context | Last updated: 2026-05-11 -->

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Rich Text rendering requires different output types depending on the target platform: a Java server app needs an HTML string; an Android app needs either a `CharSequence` (Spannable) for `TextView` or a native `View` tree. Shipping a single artifact with all platform-specific code would force Android apps to pull in HTML dependencies and vice versa. It would also require Android consumers to deal with the full Java SDK dependency graph even if they only need Android output.

The initial commit already separated HTML rendering as a distinct module (`html`) from the core pipeline, and the Android module followed shortly after.

## Decision

Organize the project as a Gradle multi-module build with three published artifacts:

- **`core`** — the abstract rendering pipeline (`Processor`, `Renderer`, `RenderabilityChecker`, `Context`, `Simplifier`). No platform-specific code. Dependency: `contentful.java` SDK + `jsr305` only.
- **`html`** — extends `core` to render Rich Text to HTML strings. Additional dependency: `commons-text` for HTML entity escaping.
- **`android`** — extends `core` to render Rich Text to `CharSequence` (Spannable) or Android `View` trees. Additional dependencies: `androidx.appcompat`, `androidx.cardview`, Robolectric (test).

An `android_sample` module exists for demonstration but is not published.

## Consequences

- **Enables:** Consumers include only the artifact(s) they need. An Android app that wants native views only needs `android` (which transitively brings `core`); it never touches `html`.
- **Enables:** Clear separation of concerns — `core` can be extended for any output type (e.g., a future `markdown` module) without touching existing modules.
- **Accepted trade-off:** Version coordination across modules requires updating multiple `build.gradle` files and all README dependency snippets on each release. This is currently a manual process.
- **Accepted trade-off:** The multi-module structure requires Android SDK tooling even for developers only working on `core` or `html`, because `settings.gradle.kts` unconditionally includes `android`.
